newsitem.title: USA: Enron, Oregon utility merger wins support.
newsitem.headline: Enron, Oregon utility merger wins support.

text.p: Enron Corp said Wednesday several environmental and public interest groups agreed to support its merger with Portland General Corp in return for commitments to various environmental and pro-competition intiatives.

The groups, which include the Natural Resources Defense Council and Trout Unlimited, have pledged to urge the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC) to approve the merger, the companies said in a release.

"After listening to each others' concerns, PGC and Enron are able to offer these groups a package of measures that gives them the assurances they needed...," said Alvin Alexanderson, senior vice president of Portland General.

If the merger goes through, the utility and Enron agreed to acquire renewable resources, secure funding for conservation and investigate and propose rate structures for residential customers and low-income customers.
Some consumer groups have formally protested the merger on the grounds that it does not assure significant benefits to existing utility customers.
The merger is also opposed by other utilities in the West which argue that the purchase of Portland General by Enron would limit rather than expand market competition.
The staff of the OPUC is expected to make a preliminary report on the merger proposal January 16.
